title: Larkspur round one
eyebrow: ARCS Field OS · Pre-call · Product lead, payments, 1 of 3
sub: Thu 12 Nov, 2:00 to 2:45 ET. Interviewer billed as Morgan Reyes (VP Product, unverified). Fictional example. Two jobs, in order: confirm this is real, then win the round.
when: Thu 12 Nov · 2:00 to 2:45 ET · Zoom via the recruiter's invite

pinned.label: Frozen · 11:40 PM ET Wed
pinned.text: Past this point, more polishing is soothing, not preparing. Tomorrow: say the three cockpit lines out loud once, and check Gmail for Dana's reply at 1:30.

checks.evidence: The recruiter named the client in her first message (Tue 10 Nov 9:12 ET).
Role listed on the company's own careers page, checked Tue 10 Nov 9:40 ET. Sent a one-page CV only.
Invite came from a company-domain address; DMARC pass in the headers (Wed 11 Nov 14:05 ET).
Identity questions open the call: tenure, team, the product's name.
Every verification ask answered within a day.

sections.title: 1 · Tripwires: always on, leave the call

items.lede: Any request to install, update or fix your camera, mic or meeting app.
bullets: Join in the browser only.
The link must land on zoom.us.

items.lede: ID, SSN, bank or wallet details, or any payment.
bullets: A first-round interview needs none of these.

items.lede: A move to Telegram or WhatsApp, or a repo or tool to open.
bullets: Fake-interview campaigns use a take-home repo to deliver malware.

sections.title: 2 · Ask first: minutes 0 to 4, proof it's real

items.lede: Which product line is this, and who leads it today?
bullets: This is the identity check. A specific, checkable answer is a pass.
Generic or "confidential for now": re-ask once, plainly.
Strongest proof: ask for a work email to send a thank-you. A company-domain address settles identity.

items.lede: Who does the role report to? How big is the team?
bullets: A real org chart is hard to fake.
Tells you whether the job is the right shape for you.

items.lede: Is there a pager rotation for product leads?
bullets: The likely deal-breaker. Settle it before investing more rounds.

sections.title: 3 · Decide: go or stop by minute 20

items.lede: The team is named with specifics, or a company-domain address arrived.
bullets: Run the interview lane.

items.lede: Neither by minute 20, or the answers are scripted deflection.
bullets: Finish politely.
Send nothing further.
Ask the recruiter in writing who you met.

sections.title: 4 · Say: once the person checks out

items.lede: Payments product lead. Moving money safely is the work.
bullets: Two launches under a money-transmitter license, zero regulator findings.
Bridge: that is the core problem a payouts product has to get right.

items.lede: Owned the payouts roadmap from pilot to general availability.
bullets: Say the volume you can source; skip the ones you cannot.
Product person, not a payments engineer.

sections.title: 5 · Close: one next step before you hang up

items.lede: Before we go, can we name one next step? Action, owner, date.
bullets: Mine: send the payouts case study by Thursday.
Ask theirs: who decides on the next round, and by when.
If they will not name one, that is the answer. Log it, do not push.

lanes.title: Before
lanes.job: Settle who you're meeting. Nothing here is for saying out loud.

cards.title: Status
cards.stamp: Checked in Gmail 11:30 PM ET Wed. Re-check at 1:30.
rows: Sent 4:10 PM ET Wed: asks Morgan's title and work address, and the team name.

cards.title: Who is Morgan Reyes
rows: A Morgan Reyes lists VP Product at Larkspur on a professional profile; no company page names them.
The recruiter named the title; nothing first-party confirms it.

cards.title: Recruiter
rows: Agency domain resolves, long posting history, asked you to run nothing.
First contact came from a personal address.

cards.title: Odds
rows: ~70% legit as described, ~20% legit with wrong details, ~10% impersonation. Error bars about ±15.
A company-domain address drops impersonation under 5%. A dodge on the team name pushes it past 30%.

cards.title: Checks you can still run
items: Reverse-image the interviewer's profile photo (Google Lens, TinEye).
Confirm the invite link lands on zoom.us before joining. Join in the browser.

lanes.title: Opening
lanes.job: Confirm the person before you perform.

cards.title: First five minutes
rows: Hellos. Ask open: how long have you been at Larkspur, and which team are you on?
Ask the product line and who leads it today.

cards.title: How to read the answers
items: Pass: specific texture you could check later, or an honest "I'm not sure, I'll find out".
Soft flag: fluent but generic on the team's name. Re-ask once, plainly.
Fail: agreeing with whatever you suggest, camera off with a looping script, or any push toward a tripwire. Apply the stop rule.

lanes.title: Interview
lanes.job: Show product leadership on regulated payments, with examples.

cards.title: Run of show
rows: Their questions: roadmap, cross-functional delivery, risk and compliance, examples.
Case, if it comes: a payouts failure and how you would find it.
Your questions 4 to 7 below. Close on round two.

cards.title: What they test
rows: Requirements into product across design, engineering, risk

cards.title: Roadmap method
rows: Compliance as co-designer at sprint planning.

cards.title: Delivery story
cards.text: We mapped dependencies before committing to dates, and the same team shipped the second launch in half the time of the first.

cards.title: Your questions 4 to 7
items: Live with customers, or pre-launch? Which markets first?
Who owns compliance, and how early are they in planning?
What does round two cover, and who runs it?
What does success look like at six months?

cards.title: Don't
items: Renegotiate comp in round one, or mention other roles or candidates.
Supply the answer to your own check ("you're on the payments team, right?").

lanes.title: Debrief
lanes.job: Score before memory rewrites it, then close the loop.
